subject: Recap: Pilot affordability window & batching/cache ops
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Pilot affordability window & batching/cache ops

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the 30m earlier. Quick recap below so we have alignment on pain, goals, and immediate next steps. I included Marissa and Ben to help scope the pilot and ops checklist.

What we heard (pain points)
- Token spend volatility: monthly bills swing 2-3x depending on weekend traffic and a single bad prompt pattern.
- Peak latency spikes on NLU endpoints (affecting customer flows) — target is 99th pctl < 300ms.
- Engineering bandwidth: your infra team wants a minimally invasive pilot (no major infra refactor).
- Budget guardrail: procurement can approve a pilot up to ~$40k over 3 months; anything above needs finance pre-approval.

Goals for pilot (agreed)
- Demonstrate sustained per-request cost reduction of 40–60% vs current hosted runs for the same quality.
- Keep 99th pctl latency within 300–350ms for production-like traffic.
- Produce an ops runbook so your infra team can accept traffic after pilot (SLOs, fallback behavior).

Primary levers we proposed
1) Batching + concurrent-shard tuning: conservative starting point = batch size 6; ramp to 12 depending on latency curve. Expected cost delta: ~-25% at batch=6, -40% at 12 for your workload mix (see attached CSV).
2) Prefix/KV caching for frequent user prompts: reduces repeated prefix compute; expectation ~-10–15% savings for conversational flows.
3) Lightweight quantization on a candidate model variant to trim cpu/gpu cycles during token generation (~-15% cost).
4) Dedicated pilot capacity (2 GPUs) for predictable throughput during peak windows; fallback to compatible hosted model when capacity constrained.

Initial numbers (very rough)
- Current avg cost per 1k tokens (est): $0.85
- Projected avg cost per 1k tokens with batching + cache + quantization: $0.34–0.48
- Pilot budget ask: $30k–$40k over 8–12 weeks (includes infra + 3 pilot iterations + engineering support)

Open questions / asks from FolioPay
- Confirm whether finance can sign off on the $40k pilot threshold by next Wed (2026-05-26).
- Your infra team: can they join a short ops readiness call? Ben — can you own the checklist and preflight?
- Clarify traffic window you'd like us to mimic (peak hourly RPS + average sequence length) so we can size batch policy.

Attachments: pilot-estimate-v2.csv (cost scenarios), example-prompt-set.txt (redacted sample prompts).

Next steps
- Olga: send updated estimate + ops checklist (today) — ACTION: done (attached).
- Sofia: confirm budget gate decision and provide peak traffic numbers (by 2026-05-26).
- Schedule: Marissa to propose pilot start dates after budget confirmation.

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call to walk through the CSV if helpful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Olga — useful summary. A couple of quick clarifications: 

1) ROI timeframe: our CFO wants a conservative 6-month window to understand when unit economics hit break-even post-integration. Can you provide a 3- and 6-month ROI table (run-rate vs one-off integration costs)?

2) Latency sensitivity: our checkout NLU path absolutely cannot go above 350ms 99th pctl during the pilot window. If batching risks pushing beyond that, we need a hard fallback policy and clear rollback steps.

3) Ops readiness: platform-ops wants a one-pager checklist and a 30m runbook walkthrough before cutover. They may ask for an on-prem reference if the availability/latency charts look risky.

We can confirm budget gate by 2026-05-26 — I’ll loop in procurement but please include a short bulleted payment/contract path so they can see options (month-to-month vs committed).

Sofia Morales
Head of Platform Engineering | FolioPay
s.morales@foliopay.com

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and the constraints — all helpful. Answering inline: 

1) ROI tables: attached a new tab in pilot-estimate-v2.csv with 3- and 6-month run-rate vs one-time integration assumptions. The conservative 6-month scenario shows breakeven at ~5 months based on your current traffic mix and our baseline savings assumptions.

2) Latency & fallback: agreed on hard SLO. Ben will own a rollback playbook; operationally the plan is: start at batch size 6 with aggressive latency monitoring, automated throttle at 95th pctl breach to drop batching to 2, then failover to a smaller (faster) model variant if 99th pctl remains >350ms for more than 2 consecutive 10-minute windows. We'll document the exact metrics and runbook in the ops one-pager.

3) Ops readiness: Ben will send the one-pager by EOD Wed (05/20). We can do the 30m walkthrough the week of 05/24 — booking link here: https://calendly.com/redwood/30-min-demo.

Budget path: we can offer month-to-month pricing for pilot or a 3-month committed pilot (5% discount). I attached a very short SOW template Marissa will flesh out; procurement should be fine seeing those two options.

Proposed next step: Sofia to confirm budget gate by 05/26; if yes, we lock an early pilot start of 06/08.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the CSV update and the SOW draft.

Best,
Olga
